name: Harvey
tagline: The legal-AI leader that went from law-firm copilot to most valuable company in legal AI
shortSummary: Harvey is the San Francisco AI platform for legal and professional services, founded in 2022 and now the most valuable and best-funded company in legal AI. It trains its own open-weight legal models.

facts.label: Founders
facts.value: Winston Weinberg (ex-O'Melveny & Myers); Gabriel Pereyra (ex-DeepMind / Google Brain / Meta AI)

facts.label: Sector
facts.value: Legal AI / AI for professional services

facts.label: Product
facts.value: AI copilot + workflow for law firms; Harvey Tenet (open-weight legal model, 2026)

facts.label: Status
facts.value: Private; four acquisitions in 2026 incl. Guardrails AI

rounds.label: Seed
rounds.note: Early backing anchored by the OpenAI Startup Fund (with angel Jeff Dean and Elad Gil), before the product's public launch. Amount ~US$5M per trackers.

rounds.label: Series A
rounds.note: Led by Sequoia — Harvey's first widely announced round.

rounds.label: Series B
rounds.note: Kleiner Perkins and Sequoia led, valuing the two-year-old startup at US$715M.

rounds.label: Series C
rounds.note: Led by GV. The Information had reported Harvey sought ~US$600M at a US$2B+ valuation to acquire legal-research service vLex; those plans fell through, producing this smaller Series C.

rounds.label: Growth Round
rounds.note: Reported mid-2025 round led by Kleiner Perkins and Coatue, tripling the valuation to US$5B. (Multiple further secondary/extended rounds moved Harvey's reported valuation through ~US$8B during late 2025 — third-party tracker reports vary.)

rounds.label: Series G
rounds.note: Led by GIC with Sequoia and Kleiner Perkins, pricing Harvey at US$11B six months before the September round (matches Frontier Rounds' Funding Leaderboard snapshot).

rounds.label: New Round
rounds.note: Co-led by Lightspeed and Diffusion, a new firm co-founded by Kris Fredrickson (a longtime Harvey backer who previously invested via Coatue). Announced together with the acquisition of Guardrails AI (AI-agent security; Harvey's fourth acquisition of 2026). Harvey has now raised more than US$1.5B in total.

sections.heading: From Roommate Demo to Legal AI's Biggest Company
sections.body: Pereyra showed Weinberg OpenAI's GPT-3 and Weinberg — a former O'Melveny & Myers securities litigator — realized it could transform legal workflows. The two launched Harvey in 2022, and the startup became the category's defining vendor: by September 2026 it counted ~80% of top US law firms as customers, and its valuation has risen from US$11B (March) to US$15.6B (September), a 42% jump in six months with revenue roughly doubling over the same period.

sections.heading: Own the Model, Own the Category
sections.body: Harvey's 2026 strategy shift is toward its own models: weeks before the September round it launched Harvey Tenet, its first post-trained open-weight legal model (based on Moonshot's Kimi K3), trained specifically for legal tasks. The US$550M round is earmarked for model talent and compute — moving beyond building on top of OpenAI/Anthropic models.

sections.heading: Four Acquisitions and a Platform Play
sections.body: The Guardrails AI deal (agent-security testing, co-founders Shreya Rajpal and Zayd Simjee joining Harvey's product org) is Harvey's fourth acquisition of 2026. Founder Weinberg says more are likely, treating deals largely as acqui-hires for strong teams — a consolidation pattern that matches Lightspeed's view that legal is the second-largest addressable AI market after code.

sections.heading: A Valuation Justified by Market Size
sections.body: Lightspeed estimates legal is the second-largest addressable AI market, and that market argument underpins the ~US$15.6B valuation. With >US$1.5B raised, Harvey is simultaneously the most valuable and best-funded company in legal AI — the reference point against which every legal-AI competitor (Legora, Robin AI, Spellbook, etc.) is now measured.
